answer: Each agent key must hold its own 64 GB sealed replica of a beacon-seeded dataset, call it the juniper set, and pass a random storage audit every epoch. Sealing takes hours and the replica is bound to that key, so two keys cannot share one disk. A farm of n keys pays for n x 64 GB of live storage plus a fresh reseal whenever it fails an audit. Reward nectar only flows through the audit inlet after a passing proof, so a lapsed key earns nothing.
